To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the coverage of mass drug administration (MDAs) with antibiotics for trachoma in Nigeria was lower than expected and that the coverage reported by community health volunteers was not accurate.

1) The coverage of mass drug administration (MD) was 60.3%, which was less than the minimum 75% coverage target; 2) The coverage reported from administrative reports of the program was 75.8%, which was greater than the coverage from our survey; and 3) The discrepancy was largely due to the identification of communities missed in the MDA, and not reported in community directed distributor (CDD) registers.

the MDA coverage in the Plateau State, where CDDs were used for the first time to deliver trachoma MAs, was lower than the target coverage, the observed discrepancy between the reported coverage from administrative reports and the actual coverage was mainly due to identification of missed communities and not reporting of the MDA in the registers, and that the CRS for evaluation of MDAs is an additional tool that can be used to monitor the MDA and to identify the communities that have been missed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evaluation of the effectiveness of the mass drug administration (MDAs) for trachoma in Nigeria, which is part of the global effort to eliminate trachoma by the year 2020.
the monitoring and evaluation of mass drug administration for the treatment of trachoma.
the monitoring of mass distribution interventions for trachoma in Plateua State, Nigeria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CRS provides a useful additional method to evaluate the coverage of MDA for trachoma.

the CRS provides a useful additional tool to CDD register data for MDA monitoring, and that the data from this survey suggest that the MDA was not delivered in some communities, and that the CDD register data are not comprehensive.
the CRS is a useful additional tool in the evaluation of MDA and the CDD registers should be used in conjunction with the CRS to provide an accurate assessment of MDA coverage in Plateau State.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the CRS was a useful additional monitoring and evaluation tool that provided a more accurate picture of MDA coverage than the CDD registers and that there is a need to improve the training of CDDs in the future to ensure better MDA coverage.
the use of CDD registers for monitoring MDA coverage is insufficient to provide accurate coverage estimates.
the CRS is a good tool to monitor the MDA coverage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CDD system is not working as well as it could.

the CDD network is a good platform for delivery of trachoma MAs in Plateau state, Nigeria, but that the coverage is lower than reported and that the coverage is likely lower than the minimum target of 80%.
the CRS is an excellent way to monitor coverage of mass drug administration.
